newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill recpurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Wednesday fanned by a large number of new domestic A share issue this week, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 11.50 percent from 10.35 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 7.8 million lots from 6.5 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
A dozen firms are issuing A shares this week as part of Beijing's efforts to cool overheated stock markets.
"Big institutions borrowed heavily on the repurchase market in order to purchase the new issues, which pushed up the repo contracts," said a trader.
"The rates will linger around the current high level in the short-term due to heavy new share issues," he said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Wednesday with the new A share issues draining funds on the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 120.85 yuan from 121.04 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market was almost unchanged at 1.1 million lots.
Traders said investors were selling their spot state debt contracts to raise cash to bid for new A share offers on the domestic market.
The contracts are likely to move in a narrow range in slow trading in the short term, they said.
